summary: Counter-Strike franchise entries added as supplemental sourced guide rows; Sami did not list these in the locked personal spine.

entries.title: Counter-Strike

primary.why: The original Counter-Strike released commercially on Windows, later reaching Xbox, OS X, and Linux. Windows remains the best archive route because it is the primary PC version with the strongest compatibility, server, mod, and capture path.
primary.how_to_play: Use the Steam Windows release of Counter-Strike 1.6. Document server/mod state if capturing multiplayer.

all_releases.fidelity: Primary PC route with broadest server/mod/capture support.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity and most complete preservation route.
skip: no sourced exclusive content requiring a secondary route.
skip: no sourced exclusive content over Windows.
skip: useful native route, but Windows is the default capture target.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Windows Steam release is the main archival route; no sourced platform-exclusive content is logged.

entries.remaster_caveats: Source, Global Offensive, and Counter-Strike 2 are separate entries rather than direct replacements for this legacy entry.

entries.title: Counter-Strike: Condition Zero

primary.why: Condition Zero released on Windows, later receiving OS X and Linux support. Windows is the best archive route because it includes the multiplayer, Tour of Duty, and Deleted Scenes content with the broadest compatibility/capture path.
primary.how_to_play: Use the Steam Windows release and install both Condition Zero and Deleted Scenes.

all_releases.fidelity: Primary PC route with all included modes.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity complete route.
skip: no sourced exclusive content over Windows.
skip: useful native route, but Windows is the default capture target.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Windows includes the complete Condition Zero / Deleted Scenes package.

entries.remaster_caveats: Condition Zero is a distinct entry, not a replacement for Counter-Strike 1.6.

entries.title: Counter-Strike Neo

emulation.notes: Original arcade hardware preferred; unofficial dumps are not the archive recommendation.

primary.why: Counter-Strike Neo was a Japan-only arcade adaptation published by Namco on Linux-based arcade hardware. No home port is sourced, so the original arcade route is the archive target.
primary.how_to_play: Use an original Counter-Strike Neo arcade setup if available; document cabinet/hardware state and service limitations.

all_releases.reason: primary: only official release platform.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Arcade service/hardware availability limits modern play; this is a preservation entry.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official home port is sourced.

entries.title: Counter-Strike: Source

primary.why: Counter-Strike: Source released first on Windows as the Source-engine remake of Counter-Strike, then came to OS X and Linux. Windows is the best archive route because it has the broadest compatibility, server, mod, and capture path.
primary.how_to_play: Use the Steam Windows release. Document server/mod state if capturing multiplayer.

all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity complete route.
skip: no sourced exclusive content over Windows.
skip: useful native route, but Windows is the default capture target.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Windows is the fidelity and preservation route.

entries.remaster_caveats: Separate Source-engine entry, not a content-complete substitute for later CS:GO/CS2.

entries.title: Counter-Strike Online

primary.why: Counter-Strike Online is a Windows free-to-play regional spin-off for Asian markets, developed by Nexon with Valve oversight. Windows is the only sourced platform and the regional service client is the archival target.
primary.how_to_play: Use the official regional Nexon client only where service is still available; document region, service state, and client version.

all_releases.fidelity: Only sourced official platform; regional service route.
all_releases.reason: primary: only official platform, subject to service/region availability.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Service/region availability affects whether the game can be played normally.

entries.remaster_caveats: Regional service state should be verified before any capture.

entries.title: Counter-Strike: Global Offensive

primary.version: Legacy Windows release / re-listed Steam title
primary.why: Global Offensive released on OS X, PlayStation 3, Windows, Xbox 360, and later Linux. Counter-Strike 2 replaced it on Steam in 2023, but the legacy game later became accessible as a separate/legacy route with matchmaking caveats. Windows is the best archival route for CS:GO because it has the strongest capture/community-server path.
primary.how_to_play: Use the Windows legacy/re-listed Steam route where available. Expect official matchmaking limitations and document whether community servers or offline/demo tools are being used.

all_releases.reason: skip: legacy platform support was superseded by later service changes; Windows is the archive route.
skip: legacy console route and no sourced exclusive content over Windows.

all_releases.fidelity: PC legacy route with best community-server/capture path.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity archival route for CS:GO legacy state.
skip: no sourced exclusive content over Windows.
skip: useful native route, but Windows is the default capture target.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: CS2 replaced CS:GO for the live current service, while CS:GO remains an archival legacy route with matchmaking/community-server caveats.

entries.remaster_caveats: Counter-Strike 2 is the current live successor; CS:GO should be captured as a legacy service state.

entries.title: Counter-Strike Online 2

emulation.notes: Service shutdown limits preservation to captures/metadata.

primary.why: Counter-Strike Online 2 was a Windows regional service sequel for Asian markets, but its master server shut down in 2018. The Windows client is therefore only a historical preservation target.
primary.how_to_play: No legitimate current play route is sourced after the master-server shutdown; preserve client metadata, captures, and shutdown history.

all_releases.fidelity: Only sourced official platform, now service-discontinued.
all_releases.reason: primary: historical Windows service route, not a normal current play route.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Service shutdown prevents a normal play recommendation; this is a preservation entry.

entries.remaster_caveats: Master server shutdown means legitimate play is not currently possible via normal official service.

entries.title: Counter-Strike Nexon

primary.why: Counter-Strike Nexon began as Counter-Strike Nexon: Zombies, was renamed Counter-Strike Nexon: Studio, and later Counter-Strike Nexon. It is a Windows-only Steam spin-off, so Windows is the archive route.
primary.how_to_play: Use the current Steam Windows release and document current title/service state.

all_releases.fidelity: Only sourced official platform; Steam Windows route.
all_releases.reason: primary: only official release platform.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Only one official platform is sourced.

entries.remaster_caveats: Title history matters: Zombies, Studio, and current Counter-Strike Nexon are the same continuing Steam entry.

entries.title: Counter-Strike 2

primary.why: Counter-Strike 2 released for Windows and Linux as the Source 2 successor/update to Global Offensive. Windows is the best archive route because it has the broadest compatibility, capture, and competitive ecosystem support.
primary.how_to_play: Use the current Windows Steam release. Document patch, map pool, and live-service state at capture time.

all_releases.fidelity: Current Source 2 PC route with broadest capture/competitive support.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity current route.
skip: useful native route, but Windows is the default archive capture target.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: CS2 is the current fidelity/live-service route, but it removed or changed some CS:GO-era features; capture CS:GO separately for legacy preservation.

entries.remaster_caveats: No macOS release is sourced; CS2 replaced CS:GO as the live main service and should be captured with patch context.
